key_insight: Extending BK19 with two blending switches enables quasi-geostrophic dynamics within the same discretization used for compressible, pseudo-incompressible, and hydrostatic flow.
engineering_relevance: A unified solver can represent fast compressible dynamics and slow balanced flows without requiring a separate quasi-geostrophic code.
method: Apply small-Rossby-number asymptotics to the fully discrete semi-implicit finite-volume scheme.
Construct a consistent staggered-grid curl operator and recover the QG pressure Poisson equation.
Add switches for the pressure equation and prognostic versus geostrophically diagnosed horizontal momenta.
evidence_signal: Two idealized vortex tests assess QG vortex stability and show convergence of compressible solutions toward slow, balanced QG dynamics as the Rossby number decreases.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two idealized vortex cases; robustness for more complex flows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver
